description.narrative:
Church of Sweden, (CoS) and Norweigan Church Aid (NCA) have submitted a common programme proposal "Peace building in Ethiopia 2019-2020".
With reference to the Strategy governing the Swedish development cooperation with Ethiopia 2019-2020 and the strategy goal "Streghthen democracy, gender equality and increased respect for human rights" Sida will decide to support the programme with a total budget of 15,5 MSEK. Sida will finance the programme with 9 MSEK and Norway with 6,5 MSEK. Norway will beside the common programme also financa an Eritrea component. Norway and Sweden will have two separate agreements. Act CoS will be the agreement partner to Sida and NCA will be the principal implementer on the ground in Ethiopia together with 6 other Ethiopian partners.
The over all goal for the programme is to make the Ethiopian society more inclusive on woman and youth, more cohesive and advancing towards sustainable peace. The proposed programme will enable and mobilize religious actors/men /women and youth to promote social cohesion in Ethiopia, to build peace and to strengthening conflict handling mechanisms. The estimated time for implementation is 3 years which starts with a one year inception phase. The budget is about 9 MSEK. The programme is to be implemented on both national and local level. The main target group is religious actors, woman, men and youth representing faith communities and who are in a position to motivate and engage in promotion of social cohesion and conflict reducing work. The programme will focus on youth, both female and male and will aim to involve women in peace building processes. The program will also involve local, federal, and national administration, media practitioners, political actors, traditional leaders, religious leaders and by the government established peace building structures including the newly created Ministry of peace for example. The final beneficiaries of the the programme will be the communities and populations in the target areas.

Svenska Kyrkan (SvK) har genom sin internationella verksamhet ansökt om stöd för programmet "Fredsbygge i Etiopien 2019-2022" tillsammans med Norweigan Church Aid (NCA).
Med hänvisning till Strategi för Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete med Etiopien 2016-2020 och särskilt strategimålet "Stärkt demokratisering, jämställdhet och ökad respekt för mänskliga rättigheter" avser Sida att besluta om att finansiera programmet med en total budget om ca 15,5 MSEK. Där Sida kommer att finansiera 9 MSEK och Norge ca 6,5 MSEK av programmet. Norge kommer dessutom att finansiera en Eritreakomponent (utanför den angivna budgeten) som Sverige inte kommer att bidra till om 3 MNOK. Norge och Sverige kommer att ha var sitt avtal. Sida kommer att ingå avtal med SvK som kommer vidareförmedla pengar till NCA som i sin tur vidareförmedlar medel till 4 av de 6 Etiopiska partners (trossamfund) som ska implementera programmet. Dessa har valts ut som lämpliga pga. deras storlek och breda närvaro i det Etiopiska samhället. Implementeringen ska ske i områden runt om i Etiopien som är särskilt drabbade av våldsamma konflikter och där trossamfunden förväntas kunna ha en positiv inverkan. Dessa områden kommer närmare att analyseras och slutligen bestämmas under det inledande året av programmet.
Det övergripande målet för programmet är att göra det etiopiska samhället mer inkluderande för kvinnor och ungdomar, uppnå social samexistens/samförstånd och ta steg mot hållbar fred. Programmet kommer att implementeras både på nationell och lokal nivå. Den primära målgruppen är religiösa ledare, kvinnor, män och ungdomar som representerar olika trossamfund och har möjlighet att påverka samhället i en inkluderande och fredlig riktning. Programmet verkar uttryckligen för att få med kvinnor och ungdomar i det fredsbyggande arbetet och inkluderar aktörer på nationell, federal och lokal nivå såsom media, politiker, traditionella ledare, religiösa ledare samt fredsbyggande aktörer som regeringen format såsom fredsdepartementet (Ministry of Peace). Den slutliga målgruppen som förväntas dra förmån av programmet är samhällen och befolkningen i de områden där programmet implementeras och ytterst hela den Etiopiska befolkningen.

The overall goal for the programme is that the Ethiopian society will be more inclusive regarding women and youth, more cohesive and advancing notably towards sustainable peace. Outcomes of the intervention in order to achieve the overall goal are: Outcome 1: religious actors promote social cohesion, peace and reconciliation on local and national levels. Outcome 2:Women's participation and influence in promoting social cohesion, peace and reconciliation on local and national levels has increased. Outcome 3: Increased participation and influence of youth in peace processes Outcome 4: The programme providers capacity and quality of interventions are enhanced The ultimate beneficiaries of the programme will be the communities and populations in the target areas who will both develop their vision of a peaceful community and benefit from peaceful and inclusive co-existence between various groups and the advantages emanating from a peaceful society.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
This Peace Building Program funded by Sweden and Norway, is a collaborative effort between Act Church of Sweden (Act CoS) and Norwegian Church Aid (NCA). The program, which was officially launched on September 1, 2019, aimed to achieve four interconnected outcomes related to social cohesion, peace, and reconciliation engaging interfaith actors, women and youth in faith. It was implemented in partnership with four local Faith-Based Organizations (FBOs), namely, Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahido Church Development and Interchurch Aid Commission (EOTC-DICAC), Ethiopian Muslims Relief and Development Association (EMRDA), Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus Peace Commission (ECCMY-PC), and the Inter-Religious Council of Ethiopia (IRCE). The programe was implemented in four regions (Amhara, Oromia, Gambella and parts of Afar regions). The programme has directly reached to more than 58,000 people (out of which 45% being Women), while over 1.1 million people (out of which 47% were Women) were indirectly reached through the local peace structures in the target areas.
The main objective of the project was to facilitate and promote social cohesion, peace, and reconciliation through building intervention capacities of various peace structures, where faith actors, women, and youths make up of these groups. Specifically, the project aimed at increasing the participation and influence of faith actors, women, and youths through enhancing implementing partners', peace structures', and other community structures' capacities for quality project intervention, dialogue and consultations, and peacebuilding. Capacity building, establishing/strengthening peace structures, dialogue and consultation were key strategies employed to transform activities into outcomes.
Over the course of three and half years, the program has made significant strides in achieving its objectives as described in the Final Programme Report. Some of the major achievement seen through this intervention, can be summarised as follows:
As a result of this intervention, in various target areas, diverse religious actors are working together as one entity promoting social cohesion, peace and reconciliation. Some of these behavioural changes are shown in the joint celebration of religious festivities (Muslims, Christians, etc), joint messages denouncing violence and war, joint peace messages in Churches, Mosques, schools and in other public spaces and joint advocacy on issues of common concern. This is primarily the result of increased mutual trust, awareness on peace and reconciliation issues among religious actors. For ex. the religious leaders in Gasera, supported by EMRDA jointly advocating to secure land for worship for Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus, is one symbolic example of social cohesion within the context of Muslim dominance in the area. However, given the volatile conflict context in the country and involvement of various actors, close follow up and support is required to sustain these impacts.
Furthermore, visible impact was documented in the report showing the result of this intervention in strengthening women's participation. For ex. womens role as key peace actors is recognized by faith actors including men and traditional leaders, women are actively engaging and influencing peace and reconciliation processes in different project locations; women are included in all local peace structures taking leadership positions with men; women alone peace groups were also established and actively engaging in peace and reconciliation processes.
Despite that it takes more time to see deep and sustained impact, there were also sufficient documented evidence showing the program has impacted the youth to participate and influence peace and reconciliation processes in the target areas. Some of the key examples include youth in all of the project locations being organized in peace groups and engaged in diverse activities such as interfaith youth city cleaning demonstrating unity, and using social media and digital platform conveying messages on peace. As a result of this intervention, the local peace committees besides resolving conflicts, were also actively involved in conflict prevention activities in the target areas. One best example of this was how the Peace Committee from Kofele Woreda in collaboration with the peace committee and religious actors in Shashemene town played a crucial role in averting the conflict that was orchestrated to start in Shashemene in retaliation to the mob attack on a mosque in Gondar town in April 2022.
At the national level, joint peace messages were organised by interfaith leaders to show solidarity and promote the social cohesion on pertinent issues, such as violence, assassinations, war, election and the like, which otherwise would be used and lead to a further divide in the society while damaging the social cohesion.The interventions have created trust among youth and motivation to act together irrespective of their differences. However, it should also be noted that in all project locations, youth unemployment is the biggest challenge making the youth vulnerable to manipulation from different actors. Therefore, it is key that the future programming should link peace initiatives for youth with development interventions to ensure sustainable impacts.
Furthermore, as per the endline evaluation, several unintended results that affected the program were also exhibited, where one is related to the level of trust all conflicting parties had put in the FBOs. EMRDA and EOC-DICAC are worth mentioning as FBOs in this regard. EMRDA earned a high level of acceptance among the Christian denomination while EOC-DICAC earned similar acceptance among Muslims within a short time.
Another frequently reported unintended consequence of this intervention was community members' assertiveness in dealing with rumors and divisive messages that could deteriorate the social cohesion. Finally, the other unintended result of this programme was the speed at which Christians and Muslims have started to reintegrate and support each other in building churches and mosques in two of the target areas (Kemise town and Bale zone).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
